sections.heading: Keep the meaning and key word
sections.explanation: Identify a fixed phrase and check what is already printed around the gap. Useful patterns include account for, whet somebody’s appetite, be averse to + -ing, acquaint somebody with, make amends, go without saying, approve of + -ing, have access to, take into consideration, take for granted and keep an eye on. These are drawn from exercise 23; completed models below use suggested answers.
examples:
The suspect could not explain why he had sand in his boots.
The suspect could not account for the sand in his boots.

What he told me made me very curious to hear the rest of the story.
What he told me whetted my appetite for the rest of the story.

I don’t mind staying in on a Saturday night if I have good company.
I’m not averse to staying in on a Saturday night if I have good company.

Miss Hayes will explain the day-to-day running of the office to you.
Miss Hayes will acquaint you with the day-to-day running of the office.

I don’t know how I can make it up to you for spoiling your plans.
I don’t know how to make amends for spoiling your plans.

It is a foregone conclusion that Mark will get the job.
It goes without saying that Mark will get the job.

Our teacher doesn’t like it when we leave the classroom without asking first.
Our teacher does not approve of us leaving the classroom without asking first.

Those official files cannot be seen by the public until the end of the decade.
The public will not have access to those official files until the end of the decade.

Being her only niece, Ann is very precious to her.
Being her only niece, Ann is the apple of her eye.

You need to consider the fact that he hasn’t spoken French for years.
You need to make allowances for the fact that he hasn’t spoken French for years.

Sheila was the only one who came up with a solution to the problem.
Only Sheila succeeded in finding a solution to the problem.

I was surprised not to see Meg at the party but I later heard she was ill.
I was surprised that Meg was not at the party but apparently she was ill.

I know this route looks dangerous but I can’t think of a better option.
However dangerous this route looks, there is no better alternative I can think of.

Because of the lack of co-operation, he decided to leave the project unfinished.
He chose to abandon the project due to lack of co-operation.

Helen won’t be happy till she gets a full refund.
Nothing less than a full refund will satisfy Helen.

I always think about transport costs when job hunting.
I always take transport costs into consideration when job hunting.

Becky didn’t tell you because she assumed you already knew.
Becky didn’t tell you because she took it for granted that you already knew.

How would you deal with such a challenge?
What would you do if presented with such a challenge?

The neighbours will look after our house while we are away.
The neighbours will keep an eye on our house while we are away.

sections.heading: Choose the right meaning and combination
sections.explanation: Dodge is suitable for avoiding a physical obstacle; shirk collocates with duties. Affect describes an effect on something; influence can take somebody + to-infinitive. Authentic describes a work’s genuine origin; genuine can describe sincerity. Rich food is heavy or fatty; an extravagant gift is unusually costly. A commodity is a basic traded product. These explanations are editorial guidance based on exercise 26.
examples: A small dog went for my ankles but I adroitly managed to dodge it.
We all have to work harder because he’s always shirking his duties.
The Prime Minister managed to dodge any tricky questions.
The damp has affected his health; he’s got rheumatism.
I’m sure that living with a vegetarian has influenced me to eat less meat.
Before I pay for the painting, I need proof that it is a(n) authentic Picasso, not a copy.
He may appear to be genuine but in fact he’s a compulsive liar.
If you have stomach problems it is best to avoid rich food.
I was rather embarrassed when John gave me such a(n) extravagant gift.
The country derives the majority of its revenue from one commodity — coffee.

sections.heading: Artificial and false
sections.explanation: Artificial usually means manufactured rather than natural. False often means untrue, deceptive, mistaken or an imitation. Fixed collocations matter. Both false pearls and artificial pearls can describe imitations; the official key for exercise 27 was not supplied.

false alarm
false beard
false note
artificial limbs
artificial light
artificial flowers
false belief
artificial pearls

exercises.passage: Although it may (0) come as a surprise to many people, postal services have existed in various parts of the world for thousands of years. There is ample evidence to suggest that [1] the Assyrians and Babylonians had postal services. In China, a regular postal service was established in the seventh century BC, which attained such a high level of efficiency [2] the centuries that, some 2,000 years after its institution, it was winning the admiration of European explorers like Marco Polo. Efficient postal services were also established in the Persian and Roman empires, [3] these services were mainly confined to members of the state; private citizens had to make [4] with slaves and merchants to deliver their correspondence. In medieval Europe, official postal services were organised by emperors and the papacy. [5] as in ancient times, though, private citizens continued to entrust their correspondence [6] various travellers. It wasn’t until the fourteenth century AD that merchants — those private citizens with the greatest need for a speedy and regular exchange of correspondence — began to [7] up regular courier services. The needs of business led to the development of the postal service [8] we know it today.
